Run ESLint with --fix to auto-convert." - Auto-fix support and single-story conversion: - buildImplementsAutoFix(context, comment, storyPaths) returns a fixer only when: - storyPaths.size === 1 - exactly one @story line and at least one @req line - all @story/@req lines are in simple forms (no extra tokens) - applyImplementsReplacement() constructs a single line: - implAnnotation = `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}` - Replaces the original @story line with this @implements line. - Removes all @story/@req lines using allIndicesToRemove. - Preserves the prefix (indentation and optional '*') from the original @story line to maintain JSDoc structure. - Multi-story and mixed-annotation detection: - MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD = 1 and hasMultipleStories(storyPaths) => storyPaths.size > 1. - If hasImplements is true, processComment() reports messageId "cannotAutoFix" with data.reason = "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @implements annotations". - If hasMultipleStories(storyPaths) is true, processComment() reports messageId "multiStoryDetected". - Backward compatibility and both-format support: - processComment() returns early if !hasStory || !hasReq; comments with only @story, only @req, or only @implements are ignored by this rule. - No schema options are defined; behavior is controlled solely via ESLint severity levels, preserving underlying validation rules. - Plugin integration: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "prefer-implements-annotation" so the rule is loaded and exported. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES contains: - "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation": "warn" - configs.recommended and configs.strict both use createTraceabilityFlatConfig(); consumers can override rule severity to "off" | "warn" | "error" via ESLint config.

traceability.notes: The story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS is fully implemented. The new ESLint rule `prefer-implements-annotation` exists and is integrated into the plugin, providing optional, configurable recommendations to migrate from legacy `@story` + `@req` annotations to `@implements`. The rule detects legacy patterns, distinguishes single-story from multi-story or mixed-annotation cases, and offers a conservative auto-fix that converts eligible single-story blocks (with one or more simple @req lines) into a single @implements line while preserving JSDoc structure and ordering. Multi-story and mixed legacy/@implements scenarios are detected and reported without auto-fix. Backward compatibility is maintained: comments with only @story, only @req, or only @implements remain valid and are not reported by this rule, and existing validation rules continue to govern format and references. Comprehensive RuleTester tests verify auto-fix behavior, edge cases, and backward-compatibility, and these tests run successfully. Dedicated documentation in docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md provides a migration guide, configuration examples (off/warn/error), and transformation examples aligned with the story, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
